filename: Teaching Machine Learning for the Physical Sciences_  A summary of lessons learned and challenges.pdf
title: Teaching Machine Learning for the Physical Sciences: A summary of lessons learned and challenges
venue: Proceedings of the 2nd Teaching in Machine Learning Workshop, PMLR
code_availability: All the materials from the most recent iteration of this class are available here (just send a sharing request, so I can keep track of who has access).
testbed_rationale: This paper is a pedagogical workshop paper addressing machine learning curriculum and teaching practices in physics and astronomy, not Earth or climate system parameterization.
pain_points: Finding research-relevant datasets that are beginner-friendly yet non-trivial and realistic
Standard beginner datasets are overly curated and omit realistic data cleaning, imputing, and feature engineering challenges
Lack of pedagogical resources and trained instructors in ML for physical sciences
Difficulty integrating cross-disciplinary concepts such as uncertainty estimation and interpretability
extraction_notes: The paper focuses on machine learning education for physics and astronomy students and is marked out of scope as it does not address Earth, climate, or environmental science.
